text.en: Every cell of your body holds a nucleus and inside it thread-like chromosomes. These carry a molecule called DNA which holds the instructions for building you, and half of it came from each parent.

Chromosomes are thread-like, highly coiled chromatin fibres in the nucleus, packed with DNA, and they carry the hereditary information.
A gene is a segment of DNA responsible for inheriting a particular character, and each gene lies at a fixed position called its locus.
A chromosome has two sister chromatids joined at the centromere, where the spindle fibres attach during cell division, and the ends are protected by telomeres.
Based on the position of the centromere, chromosomes are telocentric, acrocentric, submetacentric or metacentric.
A human cell has 23 pairs of chromosomes; 22 pairs are autosomes that control body characters and the 23rd pair is the sex chromosomes.
Body cells are diploid (2n) with chromosomes in pairs, while gametes are haploid (n) with a single set.
A karyotype shows the number, size and shape of the chromosomes of an organism, drawn as an idiogram.
Watson and Crick proposed the double helix model of DNA using X-ray pictures by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.
DNA is a polynucleotide; each nucleotide has deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate and a base, which is a purine (adenine, guanine) or a pyrimidine (cytosine, thymine).
The two strands are held by hydrogen bonds with adenine pairing with thymine and cytosine with guanine, called complementary base pairing, and in humans the father's sperm carrying X or Y decides the sex of the child.

problem.en: A DNA strand has the base sequence A T G C C A. Write the complementary strand. Then find the chance of a girl and a boy from the cross XX with XY.

text.en: Pair A with T, T with A, G with C and C with G.
The complementary strand is T A C G G T.

why.en: Each base is replaced by its partner.

text.en: The mother gives only X; the father gives X or Y with equal chance.
Children are XX (girl) or XY (boy), each with probability 1/2.

prompt.en: Explain how the sex of a child is determined and why the father is responsible.

requiredIdeas.en: The mother has two X chromosomes and so all eggs carry X
The father has X and Y so sperms are X or Y
X from the father gives a girl and Y gives a boy

points.en: Gene = segment of DNA; chromosome = coiled DNA with proteins.
Humans: 23 pairs, 22 autosomes + XX or XY.
Base pairs: A with T, G with C; Watson and Crick double helix.
The sperm (X or Y) decides the sex of the child.
